what_it_does: Sparse matrix-sparse matrix multiplication (SpGEMM) is a core operation in scientific computing but runs slowly because accessing data from scattered matrix locations causes many cache misses and wastes memory bandwidth. Prior optimization work focused on simpler sparse-dense operations; SpGEMM-specific improvements are lacking. This paper applies hierarchical clustering to reorder matrix rows and organize computation by clusters, improving how often data can be reused from cache. The authors test 10 different reordering algorithms and 3 clustering strategies on 110 real matrices to identify the best approaches.
